title: ArcCivs resident health, inventory and profession skills
assumptions: This assessment isolates the resident health/inventory/skill contract against the prior ArcCivs supply and automatic-jobs behavior documented in ArcCivs/docs/storage-economy-assessment.json and ArcCivs/docs/supplies-economy-assessment.md. Production rates, work intervals, building outputs, construction costs and ordinary recruitment cost are unchanged.

Low/base/high use 1/10/16 participating cities. Each scenario tracks one resident per city-day; these are explicit sensitivity cases, not measured population, death, feeding, inventory-transfer or activity telemetry.

Illustrative replacement demand is 0/0.1/1 resident deaths requiring replacement per city-day. A replacement consumes the existing 12 BREAD from city storage, including when the hall is still a SITE; no new pioneer or founding grant is reset after death. Recruitment requires space, an available hall and sufficient stock.

Illustrative resident feeding is 0/1/4 actions per city-day. Each valid feed consumes 1 carried BREAD and restores up to 6 health only while the resident is below max health. The personal BREAD stack is capped at 16.

Illustrative resident supply and return counts are 1/4/16 one-item actions per city-day for BREAD, and 1/4/8 one-item actions for gear. Each action moves one existing plain item through the city-storage receipt; the same item is not newly issued. These gross transfer counts do not imply a change in total item stock.

On permanent death the worker and personal inventory are removed, with no native pickup or ground drops. Bread loss uses a maximum 16-item carried stack per death. Gear loss uses a maximum 8 gear items: one each of four iron profession tools and one armor item in each of four armor slots (leather or iron per slot). Actual carried quantities can be lower.

Per completed work cycle, the assigned profession gains 1 internal skill point. Ten cycles advance one level; levels 1..5 span 0..40 points, and each level above 1 adds 2 max health up to 28 from a base 20. Scenario work is 1/5/10 completed cycles per participating city-day; points can accrue to different worker-profession pairs. Each pair stops at 40 lifetime points, but other workers, professions and hired replacements have separate progression. There is no global or network-weekly cap; calculated weekly totals are illustrative activity potential, not monetary income or an unlimited stream for one worker-profession pair.

Matching held profession tools reduce incoming damage by 10%; native armor is equipped from the same carried items. Legacy cosmetic Citizens tools are not carried items and produce no items. The skill points are internal ArcCivs progression, not vanilla/player XP, Vault, tokens or a redeemable entitlement.

The new resident rules add no direct Vault, token or player-XP flow. Items have their own units; no exchange or SELL value is assumed. Existing item resale and the planned EconomyShopGUI SELL-to-contract transition are separate from this change and are not counted as new income.

Decision: keep the existing work and recruitment economy while treating personal supplies and possible death losses as item transfers/sinks and profession points as non-redeemable progression. After any separately authorized delivery, verify the active build, one-item supply/return receipts, the 16-BREAD cap and feeding, death inventory cleanup, and 12-BREAD replacement recruitment through a SITE hall. This assessment does not claim delivery, activation or client acceptance.

flows.source: ArcCivs CivsRules.supplyResident and the existing city-storage receipt
flows.basis: One existing plain BREAD moves to the resident per action; scenarios are 1/4/16 gross one-item transfer actions per city-day, within the 16-item personal stack cap.

flows.source: ArcCivs CivsRules.supplyResident(returning=true) and the existing city-storage receipt
flows.basis: One carried plain BREAD returns to city storage per action; scenarios mirror supply at 1/4/16 gross actions and do not mint items.

Each replacement costs the existing 12 BREAD; illustrative death-replacement events are 0/0.1/1 per city-day. Recruitment through the SITE hall avoids a death-recovery deadlock and grants no free worker.
Each valid feed consumes 1 BREAD for up to 6 restored health; illustrative events are 0/1/4 per city-day, only while health is below its level-derived maximum.

flows.source: ArcCivs CivsRules.hurtResident and CivsResidents inventory validation
flows.basis: Upper exposure assumes a full 16-BREAD personal stack is destroyed at each permanent death; use the same 0/0.1/1 death events per city-day. This is a maximum-carried-stack sensitivity, not measured stock.

One existing plain gear item moves to a resident per action. Scenarios are 1/4/8 gross items per city-day; the maximum personal set is four distinct iron profession tools plus one leather-or-iron item in each of four armor slots.

flows.source: ArcCivs CivsRules.supplyResident(returning=true) and the existing city-storage receipt
flows.basis: One existing carried gear item returns to storage per action; illustrative gross return actions mirror supply at 1/4/8 per city-day, with no item issuance.

flows.source: ArcCivs CivsRules.hurtResident and CivsResidents inventory validation
flows.basis: Upper exposure assumes the maximum 8-item gear set is destroyed at each permanent death, using illustrative 0/0.1/1 death events per city-day. Actual worn and held items are fewer if the resident is not fully equipped.

One internal point per completed cycle in one profession. Scenarios use 1/5/10 completed cycles per participating city-day, distributed across worker-profession pairs as needed. Each pair stops at 40 lifetime points; other workers, professions and replacements have separate progression. There is no network-wide cap, so weekly totals remain uncapped activity sensitivity.
